preconditions.description: The number of computers (n) and cables (m) must be within the given bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in input_cables)
preconditions.description: Each cable connects two computers within the valid range.
The input contains exactly m cables.

postconditions.description: The total number of cables (p) in the output must be at least the original number of cables (m).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for c, d in output_cables)
postconditions.description: Each output cable connects two computers within the valid range.

postconditions.expression: all((c, d) in input_cables or (d, c) in input_cables for c, d in output_cables if (c, d) not in input_cables and (d, c) not in input_cables)
postconditions.description: All original cables must appear in the output, either in their original or reversed direction.

postconditions.expression: all(len(adj_list[c]) % 2 == 0 for c in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For every computer, the number of cables connected to it must be even (allowing pairing). Here, adj_list[c] is the list of cables connected to computer c, considering directionality.

postconditions.expression: all(not (exists((c1, d1), (c2, d2) in adj_list[c] where c1 == c and d1 != d2 and d2 != c1) for c in range(1, n + 1)))
postconditions.description: No two cables connected to the same computer can have conflicting directions (i.e., no two cables in the same bundle can have information flowing in different directions).
The total number of cables (p) must be the minimum possible to satisfy all constraints.
